'''Baesler:''' {{legend0|#a5b0ff|40–50%}} {{legend0|#7996e2|50–60%}} {{legend0|#6674de|60–70%}} {{legend0|#584cde|70–80%}} | title = U.S. Senator | before_election = [[Wendell Ford]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Jim Bunning]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsKY}} The '''1998 United States Senate election in Kentucky''' was held November 3, 1998. Democratic incumbent [[Wendell Ford]] retired rather than seeking a fifth term in office. In the open race, Republican [[Jim Bunning]] narrowly defeated [[Scotty Baesler]]. This was the first open election for Senate in Kentucky since [[1972 United States Senate election in Kentucky|1972]] and the first open election for this seat since [[1968 United States Senate election in Kentucky|1968]]. With a margin of 0.59 percentage points, this election was the second-closest race of the [[1998 United States Senate elections|1998 Senate elections]], behind only [[1998 United States Senate election in Nevada|the election in Nevada]]. Bunning's swearing-in marked the first time since 1973 that Republicans held both United States Senate seats from Kentucky. == Democratic primary == === Candidates === * [[Scotty Baesler]], [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. representative]] from [[Lexington, Kentucky|Lexington]] * Jim Brown * [[Steve Henry]], [[Lieutenant Governor of Kentucky|lieutenant governor of Kentucky]] * Charlie Owen, businessman * Ken Buchanan Thompson * David L.
